headline: Deep learning models predict immunogenic epitopes for vaccine and immunotherapy design
label: Computational Immunogenicity Prediction
summary: Recent preprints and papers couple epitope and immunogenicity predictors with ESM2 embeddings and omics-driven target discovery for vaccine design.
synthesis: The dominant thread is machine learning prediction of immune-relevant epitopes and neoantigens for vaccine and immunotherapy design. TEIP couples omics-based OIP5 target discovery with a bidirectional LSTM immunogenicity model for glioblastoma neoantigen prioritisation. IFNg_DeepKG predicts interferon-gamma-inducing epitopes by combining ESM2 protein embeddings, a retrieval-augmented knowledge graph, and a multiscale CNN. What is new is the combination of curated biomedical knowledge graphs and protein language model embeddings with epitope-level immunogenicity prediction. Adjacent items apply related model classes elsewhere: VirSentAI uses HyenaDNA to predict human infectivity and PLAPT to rank approved drugs, MixRx fine-tunes Mistral Instruct 2.0 to classify drug combinations, and DRPMKB catalogues 193 AI drug-repositioning models. These extend the same predictive paradigm to infectivity, drug ranking, and drug-combination classification, though they do not address immunogenicity directly.
